objects.taxonomy_description: A tall, long-necked ungulate with distinctive ossicones and a spotted coat pattern, distinguishable from other large herbivores by its extreme vertical proportions.

diagnostic_checkpoints.Neck_Length: Possesses an exceptionally long neck that is significantly longer than the torso, distinguishing it from horses, camels, and other ungulates.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Head_Structure: Features paired, skin-covered bony protuberances (ossicones) on the top of the head rather than branched antlers or hollow horns.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Body_Proportion: Exhibits a steeply sloping backline where the forelegs are visibly longer than the hind legs, creating a distinct downward slope from shoulders to rump.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Coat_Pattern: Displays a mosaic of irregular, polygonal patches separated by lighter lines, which differs from the stripes of zebras or the solid colors of most other large mammals.

objects.taxonomy_description: An inanimate manufactured object characterized by artificial materials and non-biological structural features.

diagnostic_checkpoints.Material_Composition: The object exhibits synthetic textures such as molded plastic, painted surfaces, or uniform fabric rather than organic skin, fur, or scales.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Structural_Symmetry: The form displays mechanical precision, perfect symmetry, or simplified geometric shapes that lack the natural asymmetries found in living organisms.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Articulation_Joints: Visible seams, hinges, screws, or rigid connection points indicate manufactured assembly rather than biological growth or anatomical joints.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Surface_Finish: The surface shows uniform coloration, glossy reflections, or mold lines inconsistent with the variable pigmentation and texture of biological tissues.

objects.taxonomy_description: Handheld collapsible canopy mounted on a central shaft with radiating ribs. Canopy is fabric (nylon, polyester) stretched over 6-8 metal or fiberglass ribs. When open, diameter is 90-120 cm. Shaft is metal or wood with a curved or straight handle. Collapsible models fold down to 25-35 cm via a telescoping shaft and folding ribs. Canopy colors range from solid black to vibrant patterns. Tip of each rib has a small protective cap. Opening mechanism is manual (push-up) or automatic (button-activated). Ribs converge at a runner that slides along the shaft.
